specs.value: Natural volcanic soil (made in Japan for the German brand Dennerle, per the shop)
Holds pH at around 6–6.5 and lowers hardness
100% natural raw materials with trace elements and nutrients

prices.variant: 8 L, sale price (regular price 720,000 ₫), in stock

fits.fact: Made for planted freshwater tanks. It makes the water slightly acidic and soft.
Its buffering is said to let you dose more CO2 without pH falling too far.
Breeders of Caridina shrimp prefer it because it releases little ammonia at start-up compared with ADA and Tropica soils.
Aragonite or other calcareous hardscape cancels out its pH buffering, so avoid it.
The angular grains held slopes up to about 35°. They grip hardscape slightly less well than ADA Amazonia.

usage.fact: Use it straight from the bag. Do not rinse or pre-soak it.
Do not mix it with other substrates or use it with pH-lowering products.
Ammonia peaked at about 1.5–2 ppm in the first 72 hours and fell below 0.25 ppm by day 14. Cycle the tank before adding sensitive livestock.
Expect strong plant growth for about 9–12 months. After that, add liquid fertiliser to the water column. Add root tabs for crypts and swords from about month 4.
A soil bed held its structure for 14 months. In community or Neocaridina tanks it can last about 18 months before you need to replace it.
Plan on about 4 L for a 30 L tank and 8 L for a 50 L tank.

issues.fact: A reviewer complained that it was dusty and made the water very cloudy. The retailer replied that some clouding at first is normal.
In a test tank, buffering faded around month 9: KH rose to 2–3 dKH and pH settled near 6.7. Caridina keepers may need to partly replace the soil.
The same retailer's comparison article claims buffering lasts 24–30 months, which contradicts its own review. Both figures come from a single retailer's tanks.
Counterfeit or out-of-spec bags from unknown resellers may not show bad buffering until about day 14. Buy from established shops.
Stock in Vietnam is patchy: the Greendeal listing showed both sizes sold out.

alternatives.why: A premium Japanese soil that grips hardscape better, but it releases much more ammonia at start-up and costs more per litre.
Similar plant growth after 12 months. Start-up ammonia is moderate, but buffering is shorter and grains break down faster when plants are uprooted.
A much cheaper Vietnamese option (75,000 ₫ for 3 L). pH stays at 6.5–7.2, which suits mosses, ferns and Bucephalandra but not demanding plants.
